extracted.intended_audience: national securities exchanges (SROs), exchange counsel, SEC staff, and market participants evaluating or preparing non-transaction fee filings (connectivity/port fee proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and SEC submission of a proposed rule change to amend an exchange's non-transaction fee schedule (e.g., connectivity and port fees), including the legal/statutory justification, cost analysis, and implementation details. Also covers the SEC's criteria and Staff Guidance used to evaluate such filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural filing requirements under Section 19(b)(1) and Rule 19b-4
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change must be filed pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Exchange Act and Rule 19b-4 and include the Items I, II, and III (terms of substance, purpose and statutory basis, and statements prepared by the exchange). The text of the proposed rule change should be made available (e.g., on the exchange website and to the Commission's Public Reference Room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full text of the proposed rule change, file numbers, release numbers, and make the filing publicly available (PDF/XML). Prepare the filing so it can be published as an SEC notice to solicit public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Exchange Act statutory standards (Section 6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fees must be consistent with the requirements of the Exchange Act, including that exchange rules and fees be reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory (Section 6(b)(4)), protect investors and the public interest (Section 6(b)(5)), and not impose an unreasonable burden on competition or allocate unreasonable dues, fees, or other charges (Sections 6(b)(5) and 6(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how the proposed fee change satisfies these statutory standards directly and with evidence; identify and explain how the proposal is fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory and how it affects competition and investor protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces
rubrics_metrics.description: As an initial step in Staff's assessment, show whether the proposed fee is constrained by significant competitive forces in the market (market-based test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide market evidence and comparisons to demonstrate competitive constraints. If asserting competitive constraint, include direct comparisons to competing exchanges' fee schedules and explain why market participants would be able to discipline the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a detailed cost-based justification (cost analysis) as an alternative to market-based arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a competition-based showing is insufficient or not asserted, supply a comprehensive cost-based discussion demonstrating the reasonableness of the fee (expenses, allocations, projected costs/revenues, and mark-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed categories of costs (internal labor, monitoring, data center, hardware/software refresh, depreciation/amortization, vendor price increases, etc.), the methodology for allocating shared costs, projected 12‑month expenses and revenues, profit margins/mark-ups, and an explanation why costs and projections are current (e.g., 2024 budget). Update cost analyses periodically (annual review) and explain any deviations from prior filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and document an evidentiary record enabling Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchange should 'develop a record'—present factual support and reasoned conclusions in writing—sufficient to enable the Commission and Staff to review and evaluate the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply supporting exhibits, data tables, explanations of assumptions, and written conclusions so the Commission can perform its review; be prepared to respond to Staff requests for additional detail or to revise and refile with further documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain allocation methodology for shared/affiliate costs
rubrics_metrics.description: When costs are shared among affiliated markets, the filing must explain how costs are allocated among those affiliates and ensure no double-counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the allocation keys (e.g., hardware/software utilization, matching engine counts, gateway differences), percentages used, and rationale for differences across affiliates. Provide sufficient granularity to demonstrate allocations are reasonable and not duplicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare proposed fees to those of comparable exchanges (market-based comparison / parity analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how the proposed fee relates to comparable fees charged by other exchanges and whether fee parity or disparity exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific competitor fee schedules (with sections/lines), show side-by-side comparisons, and explain whether proposed fees are lower/higher and why (cost differences, service levels, historic baselines). Use published pricing examples to support claims about competitiveness or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess competitive effects and potential discriminatory impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed fee change would have anticompetitive effects, create unfair discrimination among market participants, or place the exchange at a competitive disadvantage relative to legacy exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how non-legacy vs legacy exchanges are differently affected, whether higher or lower non-transaction fees enable cross-subsidization of transaction fees, and whether the change would materially burden competition; present data or argumentation supporting these assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define precisely the services and definitions being changed in the Fee Schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the exact Fee Schedule text, definitions (e.g., MENI, 10Gb ULL connectivity, Full Service MEO Port—Bulk/Single, Limited Service MEO Port), and how access and functionality change (e.g., bifurcation of shared networks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend the Definitions and explanatory paragraphs in the Fee Schedule to clearly state what connectivity provides access to, whether access to affiliate markets is included, and any changed semantics so market participants understand scope of service being charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain fee mechanics, calculation methodology, and tier structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay out how fees are calculated (flat fee, tiered by volume, per-class, % of ADV, per-port), which customers the formulas apply to (EEMs, Market Makers, Members, non-Members), and any transition/harmonization with affiliate fee structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide formulaic descriptions and examples (e.g., $13,500/month for 10Gb ULL; Full Service MEO Port—Bulk flat fee of $7,500 for EEMs; Market Maker fees based on per-class or % ADV with specified breakpoints). Explain why the chosen calculation is reasonable and consistent with industry practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose implementation details including effective date and pro-ration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State when the fee change will become effective and how fees will be pro-rated when participants add or delete connectivity during a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If immediate effectiveness is requested, justify it; describe pro-rating formula (e.g., number of trading days credentialed divided by trading days in month × monthly rate) and how credentialing is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide revenue projections and assumptions (subscriber counts and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project 12‑month revenue from the fee change using clear assumptions, e.g., most recent completed full month revenues, number of subscribers, and sensitivity where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which months were used, how subscriber counts were estimated, whether the filing is an amendment to an existing fee (and thus does not require certain subscriber-churn analyses), and provide rationale if an IEX-style lost-subscriber analysis is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose prior related filings and iterative amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: List prior filings, withdrawals, and refiled proposals related to the subject fee to provide context for the current proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include citations to earlier SR filings and explain material changes between iterations so Staff can understand the evolution of the proposal and prior responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify differential treatment across customer classes and avoid unfair discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: If different fees apply to different classes (Market Makers vs EEMs vs non-Members), explain why the distinctions are reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide business/operational reasons (e.g., entitlement to two ports per matching engine, harmonization with affiliate practices, differing usage patterns), data supporting usage differences, and show that similarly situated participants are treated equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Staff Guidance expectations and be prepared to supply extensive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize Staff Guidance requires increased disclosures and that Staff now often requests more detailed cost/revenue information than prior market-based filings did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate iterative Staff review (suspensions, requests for additional detail) and provide extensive documentation up front (cost breakdowns, allocations, assumptions). Where helpful, request clarity from Staff about acceptable metrics (e.g., acceptable margins or required data points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with recordkeeping and other regulatory obligations referenced in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that exchanges comply with other applicable regulations referenced in the filing (e.g., recordkeeping rule 17a-1) and state that compliance where relevant to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the relevant regulatory provisions directly, explain how the exchange will continue to meet those obligations in light of the proposed change, and include any operational controls or documentation practices relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public access to proposal materials and relevant technical references
rubrics_metrics.description: Make filing materials and supporting technical references (e.g., matching engine counts, exchange technology whitepapers, price schedules of competitors) publicly available and cite them in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to exchange alerts, Excel or data files (e.g., matching engine counts), fee schedules of other exchanges, and any vendor/technical references used to justify costs so commenters and Staff can verify assertions.
